'''Muhammad Masud Ahmad''' {{small|[[Hilal-i-Imtiaz|HI]] [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz|SI]]}} ([[Urdu language|Urdu:]] '''محمد مسعود''' '''احمد'''), best known as '''Masood Ahmad''', (16 November 1943 &ndash; 29 December 2018) was a [[People of Pakistan|Pakistani]] [[theoretical physicist]] and [[ICTP Prize|ICTP laureate]] known for his work in [[Dual resonance model|dual resonance]] and [[Gabriele Veneziano|Veneziano]] model, a [[String theory|strings sting]] mathematically described the [[fundamental force]]s and forms of [[matter]] in [[quantum state]].

Having specialised in [[Quantum physics|Quantum]] and [[Statistical physics]], Ahmad assisted and took part in the development of [[Project-706|atomic bomb project]] as a member of Theoretical Physics Group in the 1970s, and participated in the development of the [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|atomic bomb programme]].<ref name=TNI/><ref name=TheNation>{{cite news|url=https://nation.com.pk/30-Dec-2018/nuclear-scientist-dr-masud-dies |title=Nuclear scientist Dr Masud dies|agency=Associated Press of Pakistan|newspaper=The Nation (newspaper)|date=30 December 2018|accessdate=19 December 2020}}</ref>

A staunch supporter of [[Nuclear power in Pakistan|nuclear power]], Ahmad has led Pakistan's delegation in many international and national forums and conferences in the issues of peaceful use of [[Nuclear power|nuclear energy]]. A student of [[Abdus Salam]], Ahmad was one of the senior scientists, despite his age, of Theoretical Physics Group – a physics group that was mandated to develop the designs of nuclear weapons.<ref>Theoretical Physics Group, a cue from Manhattan Project?, Shahidur Rehman, pp. 7–8</ref>

==Biography==
Born and educated in [[Lahore]], [[British India]], Masud Ahmad attended [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] in 1960, and completed his BSc degree in [[Physics]] under the contemporary supervision of [[Riazuddin (physicist)|Riazuddin]], followed by MSc degree in [[Mathematical physics]] from the same institution in 1966. Ahmad then travelled to United Kingdom and attended [[Imperial College London]] where he began his doctoral studies under Abdus Salam's physics group. In 1968, he did his DSc degree in Theoretical physics under Abdus Salam. His dissertation dealt with the theory of [[Chiral symmetry]] and [[Representation theory|algebraic representation]] in [[Gabriele Veneziano|Veneziano]] model – an early theory of [[strings theory|stings]].<ref>{{Cite journal| author =Masud Ahmad| year = 1968| title = Algebraic Realization of Chiral Symmetry and Veneziano Model| journal = [[Physical Review]]| volume = 23 | issue = 2 | pages = 103–105| doi =10.1103/PhysRevLett.23.103| bibcode=1969PhRvL..23..103F| last2 =Riazuddin| last3 =Ahmad| first3 =Masud}}</ref>

Masud Ahmad's lifelong friendship with Riazuddin was very important for Masud's scientific and philosophical development. It was Riazuddin who arranged summer stay with [[Ishfaq Ahmad]] in Islamabad for young Ahmad, thus orienting his science career in nuclear physics. Ahmad spent two years at Institute of Physics (IP) of [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] where he worked under [[Faheem Hussain]]'s Theoretical Physics Group.<ref>The Theoretical Physics Group at Quaid-e-Azam University's Institute of Physics (1968), Faheem Hussain, pp5</ref>

At IP, he published the theoretical work on Veneziano Model where he had used the [[Compton scattering]] to investigate [[Pions]] behaviour on the Veneziano Model. In 1970, along with [[Fayyazuddin]], he carried out the work on construction of Veneziano representation for pion photoproduction [[amplitude]], in which he predicted that, keeping the {{Subatomic particle|Pion}} and the [[Charge density|ρ]] trajectories, the zero-free parameter fits for the sum and the difference of the differential cross sections for unpolarised photons and the asymmetry function Σ({{Subatomic particle|Pion+}}+{{Subatomic particle|Pion-}}) are obtained.<ref>{{Cite journal| last1 = Ahmad | first1 =M. Masud| last2 = Fayyazuddin | author2-link =Fayyazuddin| date =3 August 1970| title = Pion Photoproduction in the Veneziano Model| journal =[[Physical Review D]]| volume =2 | issue =11  | pages = 2718–2724| doi =10.1103/PhysRevD.2.2718|bibcode = 1970PhRvD...2.2718A }}</ref>

Prior to the discovery of [[Alfvén wave]] in [[hydromagnetics]] in 1969, Ahmad was engaged as a theoretical physicist, working in the fields of [[Quantum physics|quantum]], [[Molecular physics|molecular]], and nuclear physics. In 1970, on an advice of Abdus Salam, Ahmad went to Italy to join [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) to pursue his further doctoral studies. In 1971, he was joined by Riazuddin and Abdus Salam where he contributed with them in an emerging theory of [[Quantum electrodynamics]].<ref>[https://www.dawn.com/news/786547 A leaf from history: The atomic option ] Dawn (newspaper), Published 16 February 2013, Retrieved 19 December 2020</ref>

==Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission==
{{Main|Project-706#Organization}}
After becoming an ICTP Associate, Ahmad was one of the young and senior scientists who were working in the ICTP.<ref name=ICTP>{{Cite web| last =(ICTP) | first = International Centre for Theoretical Physics | author-link =Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics | title =News from ICTP 86 - Dateline (scroll down to read News from Associates - Masud Ahmad award info)| year =1998 | url =http://prizes.ictp.it/pio/words/newsletter/backissues/News_86/dateline.html/?searchterm=Masud | accessdate =18 December 2020}}</ref> In January 1972, Abdus Salam called one of his eminent students from Italy to report to [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]]'s chairman [[Munir Ahmad Khan]].<ref>{{Cite web| last = Ahmad  | first = Mansoor|author2=Arvind Virmani| title = Background and Origins| website = Dr. Arvind Virmani and Magnum Books Pvt Ltd. | publisher = Institute for Defense Studies and Analysis (IDSA)| date = December 2006| url = https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:0zPIW_S-TyoJ:www.idsa.in/system/files/Monograph_No1.pdf+Two+Pakistani+nuclear+scientists,+Dr.+Riazuddin+and+Dr.+Masud+Ahmad&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESi8VycKTnWUvsAqIAS4lZfXu-duh6b98hH_LlomdX9K7V8JNiYeBJftSI-lIIOkbuBfcFN9WX0fhA1S9lKeMfOiwjp7eV7pa6LlortD4ip5poreMCHTxFMagu6CAMBcDUzsORSt&sig=AHIEtbQn7FobWx0miNEBfLOuOOhxnSJupw}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nti.org/e_research/profiles/Pakistan/Nuclear/chronology_1974.html |title=Nuclear Chronology 1970–1974 (October 1972) |website=[[Nuclear Threat Initiative]] |date=December 2005 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110918040826/http://www.nti.org/e_research/profiles/Pakistan/Nuclear/chronology_1974.html |archivedate=18 September 2011 }}</ref> He, along with [[Raziuddin Siddiqui]] and [[Riazuddin (physicist)|Riazuddin]] formed the ''Theoretical Physics Group'' (TPG) in PAEC, which was mandated to develop the theoretical designs of Pakistan's nuclear weapons.<ref>{{Cite web| last = Ahmad| first = Mansoor| title = Number 6| website = | publisher = Defence Journal of Pakistan| date = December 2005| url = http://www.defence.pk/forums/wmd-missiles/20255-interview-abdul-qadeer-khan.html}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> 

By 1973, the theoretical physicists from academic universities of Pakistan joined the Theoretical Physics Group, and initiated to work on developing the designs of the weapon. The Theoretical Physics Group directly reported to Abdus Salam who coordinated the research on metallurgy, weapon chemical lenses, enrichment, separation and reprocessing of the fuel.<ref>{{Cite news| last =Rahman  | first =Shahidur| title   =Abdus Salam and Pakistan's Nuclear weapons programme| publisher =Printwise publications| year =1998}}</ref>

In 1980, the TPG completed the calculations on how much radiation would be lost during the process of [[deuterium burning]] and, in 1982, the final design of the weapon was completed by Theoretical Physics Group (TPG). Under the leadership of PAEC chairman [[Munir Ahmad Khan]], the TPG's theoretical designed bomb was successfully cold tested, codename ''[[Kirana-I]]'', in 1983 near at the [[Kirana Hills]]. Masud Ahmad, and Riazuddin, had developed the capabilities for more advanced [[Nuclear weapon design|designs]] of a [[nuclear device]], and reportedly gave the any designs of the nuclear device in a month to PAEC.<ref>{{Cite journal| author = Shahid-Ur-Rehman| title =Theoretical Physics Group, A cue of Manhattan Project| journal =  Long Road to Chagai| pages =7, 38–39| date = October 1972}}</ref> Since then he has been staying at PAEC as a [[theoretical physicist]]. It was Ahmad and Riazuddin's indigenously theoretically designed nuclear devices that Pakistan under Munir Ahmad Khan tested several cold tests from 1983 to 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal| author = Shahid-Ur-Rehman| title = A Tale of Two Scientists| journal =  Long Road to Chagai| pages =38–39| date = October 1972}}</ref> Masud Ahmad was one of the invited scientists who participated and eye-witnessed the country's first successful tests, codename [[Chagai-I]], on 28 May 1998, and second test, codename [[Chagai-II]], on 30 May 1998. He was also a part of team of theoretical physicists who led the calculations of nuclear weapons yield in both places. The Theoretical Physics Group continued to develop more advanced designs for the nuclear weapons, and the FNPG kept the testings of the designs from 1983 to 1991.<ref>Science Odyssey, Samar Mubarakmand.</ref>

==Support for peaceful use of nuclear energy==
He was a vocal supporter of Pakistan's [[Nuclear power in Pakistan|nuclear energy programme]], and has been assisting the [[Government of Pakistan]] to established commercial and licensed [[nuclear power plant]]s in the country. He has also played an important role in [[IAEA]]'s nuclear policy to allow Pakistan to build nuclear power plants. He has assisted [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] chairman [[Parvez Butt]] to reach a civilian [[nuclear technology]] agreement with [[IAEA]]. In an honorary conference along with [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] chairman Parvez Butt and IAEA's delegation, Masud Ahmad said:

"There is an urgent need to disseminate related information on [[radioisotope]] based analytical techniques to end user institutions engaged in mitigation of [[marine pollution]]. The unplanned disposal of untreated industrial, domestic and agricultural wastes into seawater has led to contamination of the coastal areas of many developing countries in South Asia resulting into considerable increase in the concentration of toxic elements".<ref>{{Cite news| title = Pakistan to support IAEA's efforts for peaceful uses of nuclear technology| publisher=Pakistan Press International|date = 12 April 2004|url = http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/732051/files/presscut-2004-129.txt |accessdate=19 December 2020}}</ref>

In the end, Masud Ahmad concluded that: "''The [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] or [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] is a pioneer organisation in the peaceful uses of [[radiation]] and [[radioisotope]] techniques in the country in the field of [[life science]]s, [[hydrology]], agriculture and industry and it has acquired significant expertise and infrastructure in the field of [[Environmental isotopes|environmental isotope]] ecology''".<ref>{{Cite web| title =PAEC to generate 8,800 MW power by 2030|newspaper =The News International (newspaper)|date = 29 April 2009| url =https://www.thenews.com.pk/archive/print/173310-paec-to-generate-8800-mw-by-2030 |author=Nasim Zehra|accessdate=19 December 2020}}</ref>
